newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australian Broadcasting Corp Afternoon Update.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australian Broadcasting Corp Afternoon Update.

text.p: WOMAN DENIED CHANCE TO SUE AFTER SURGERY
The High Court has denied a woman the chance to sue for alleged medical negligence following a hysterectomy at a Queensland hospital 18 years ago.
The woman claims she agreed to undergo the operation in a Brisbane South Regional Health Authority hospital in 1979 after being told by a doctor that she would otherwise risk death.
She claims the hysterectomy was neither appropriate nor necessary and she has experienced pain ever since.
The Queensland Court of Appeal allowed the woman to pursue her claim although the action was outside the three year legal limit for such actions.
Today the High Court overturned that decision on appeal from the Health Authority.
FLINDERS UNI SEES POTENTIALLY HIGHER JOBLESS RATE
There's another forecast that the nation's unemployment rate could be edging back toward nine percent.
The director of the National Institute of Labour Studies, at Flinders University, Judith Sloan, says the jobless rate could reach nine percent by the end of the year.
She says that labour market conditions have been relatively soft or several months.
Professor Sloan says the immediate outlook is for relatively weak employment.
NEW COACH FOR ILLAWARRA STEELERS
The Illawarra Steelers rugby league team has appointed a new head coach.
Former international Andrew Farrar, will take over the first grade coaching position from Alan McMahon for the 1997 season.
Mr Farrar has 14 years experience in first grade football, playing with Canterbury, Western suburbs and the Steelers.
He's the first former Steelers player to be appointed to the position.
HOWARD INCONSISTENT ON FREE SPEECH: BOLKUS SAYS
The Federal Opposition says the Prime Minister's view of free speech is inconsistent.
Federal Shadow Attorney-General, Nick Bolkus says John Howard has been proclaiming his government as one which supports and protects free speech.
But Mr Bolkus says at the same time, the Howard Government has asked the High Court to re-open a landmark decision on freedom of political speech.
He says the government's seeking to wind back the decision, which found there was a wider freeedom to criticise politicians and people in the public eye.
Mr Bolkus say the move shows John Howard's not serious about protecting the rights of free speech.
-- Reuters Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
